name: Claim Check
job: Set what someone said beside what the record shows, with a state chip, so a reader sees at once which claims hold, which drifted, which are unchecked and which slipped.

anatomy.role: Who said it and when (mono, label step), then the claim as quoted
28 Chip: Sharp (green, proven), Degraded (gold, right size and wrong unit), Unchecked (plain), Slip (red, failed)
What the record shows, mono at the headline step, in the state colour
32 Evidence ref: the command or file that checked it
37 classes on the row: `sharp`, `degraded`, `grain` (unchecked) set the weight

states.name: Degraded
states.note: Right size, wrong unit or rounding.

states.name: Unchecked
states.note: Not checked yet: plain chip and grain, never red.

states.name: Slip
states.note: The record contradicts it (phone width: one column).

use_when: A call or a page made factual claims that can be checked against a record (git, a catalog, a source).
The reader needs to know what to correct before writing anything down.
avoid_when: Do not mark an unchecked claim red; red is only for a claim the record contradicts.
Do not use it for opinions; a take is 60 Heat take.
Colour has one meaning across the kit (arc weld spec 4.3): red a failed check, gold a limit, green proven, cyan an action or focus, plain (steel) unknown, magenta a paradox.

data.type: {who, at, said, state, value, note, ref}

access: Source order is said, state, record, so a screen reader reads the claim before the verdict.
The chip names the state in words; colour repeats it, never replaces it.
